name: Slack setup form loads in dashboard
steps: Click Agent setup (gear icon) in sidebar
expected: Slack setup form loads with App Token and Bot Token input fields, manifest copy button, and Connect button

name: Copy Slack manifest from dashboard
steps: In the Slack setup section, find the 'Copy the manifest' button
Verify clipboard contains valid JSON with bot scopes and socket mode config
expected: Manifest JSON copied to clipboard containing display_information, oauth_config with bot scopes, settings with socket_mode enabled, and event_subscriptions

name: Create Slack app from manifest on api.slack.com
expected: Slack app created successfully, lands on app Basic Information page

name: Generate App-Level Token
steps: On the Slack app page, go to Basic Information
expected: App token generated starting with xapp-1-..., token is copyable

name: Install app to workspace and get Bot Token
steps: Navigate to 'Install App' in the Slack app sidebar
Copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-...)
expected: App installed to workspace, bot token generated starting with xoxb-...

name: Connect Slack bot via dashboard form
steps: Navigate back to the dashboard → Channels → Slack
Paste the App Token (xapp-...) into the App Token field
Paste the Bot Token (xoxb-...) into the Bot Token field
expected: Slack connection succeeds, status shows connected, no error messages

name: Connect Slack bot via chat trigger
steps: Type 'connect slack' in the message input
Wait for the Slack setup card to appear inline
Fill in App Token and Bot Token
expected: Slack setup card appears inline in chat, connection succeeds after filling tokens

name: Verify bot appears online in Slack workspace
steps: Press Ctrl+K to open quick switcher
Check if the bot shows as online (green dot) or shows 'Waiting for X to start a conversation' banner
expected: Bot appears in Slack, does NOT show 'Waiting for X to start a conversation' banner (which means disconnected)

name: Send message to bot in DM and receive response
steps: In the bot's DM in Slack
Type 'Hello, are you connected?' and send
Wait up to 30 seconds for a response
expected: Bot responds with a relevant message within 30 seconds

name: Send message to bot in channel and receive response
steps: Type '@BotName what time is it?' and send
Wait up to 30 seconds for a response
expected: Bot responds in the channel with a relevant message

name: Bot creates thread reply in channel
steps: In the test channel, send a message mentioning the bot
Verify the response appears as a thread reply (not a top-level message)
expected: Bot's response is in a thread under the user's message, not as a separate top-level message

name: Thread context preserved across messages
steps: Send a follow-up message in the thread: 'What did I just ask you?'
expected: Bot's response references the previous message, demonstrating thread context is maintained

name: Thread context survives agent restart
steps: Go to the dashboard → Agent setup → click 'Restart Gateway'
Wait 15 seconds for agent to restart
Go back to the Slack thread
Send another message: 'Do you still remember our conversation?'
expected: Bot responds with awareness of previous thread context (thread cache persisted to disk and survived restart)

name: Thread reply mode defaults to 'quiet' for new connections
steps: Navigate to Channels → Slack setup form
Check the Thread Reply Mode dropdown
expected: Thread Reply Mode defaults to 'quiet' (not 'full'). Note: the 'full' option may still incorrectly say '(default)' — this is a known UI label bug

name: Intermediate messages suppressed in threads
steps: In the test channel, send a complex request that requires multi-step work
e.g. '@BotName search the web for the current weather in New York and summarize it'
Watch the thread for intermediate status/thinking messages
expected: Bot does NOT show intermediate 'thinking' or status messages in the thread — only the final response appears

name: Connect with invalid App Token
steps: Enter a valid Bot Token (or any xoxb- string)
expected: Connection fails with a clear error message about invalid App Token. No crash, no infinite loop, form remains usable

name: Connect with invalid Bot Token
expected: Connection fails with a clear error message about invalid Bot Token. No crash, no infinite loop, form remains usable

name: Connect with empty tokens
steps: Leave both App Token and Bot Token empty
expected: Form validation prevents submission, or clear error message displayed. No crash

name: Disconnect Slack integration
steps: Find and click the disconnect/remove button
expected: Slack disconnected, status shows disconnected, form resets to allow new connection

name: Reconnect after disconnect
steps: After disconnecting, re-enter the App Token and Bot Token
Go to Slack and verify bot responds to messages
expected: Reconnection succeeds cleanly, bot responds to messages in Slack

name: Bot handles message formatting — bold, italic, code
steps: In the test channel, ask the bot to respond with formatted text
e.g. '@BotName respond with a bold word, an italic word, and a code block'
Verify formatting renders correctly in Slack
expected: Bot's response shows proper Slack mrkdwn formatting: *bold*, _italic_, `code`

name: Bot handles long messages
steps: Ask the bot for a very long response
e.g. '@BotName write a 2000 word essay about testing'
Verify the full message is delivered (Slack has a 40000 char limit per message)
expected: Full response delivered without truncation or errors. If response exceeds Slack's limit, it should be split into multiple messages gracefully

name: Bot handles emoji and special characters
steps: Send: '@BotName respond with some emoji: 🎉 🚀 ✅ and special chars: <>&"'
expected: Bot processes the message without errors and responds. Special characters don't break the message or cause HTML encoding issues

name: Multiple rapid messages to bot
steps: In DM with bot, send 3 messages rapidly (within 2 seconds):
expected: Bot handles all messages without crashing or losing messages. May batch-process or respond to each individually

name: AckReaction configuration
steps: Send a message to the bot in Slack
Check if the bot reacts with the configured emoji before responding
expected: Bot reacts with the configured emoji on the user's message as an acknowledgment before sending its response

name: AckReaction with invalid emoji rejected
steps: Try to set an invalid value for AckReaction (e.g. 'not_a_real_emoji_xyz')
expected: Invalid emoji value is rejected, either on form validation or with a clear error message after save attempt

name: Reply mode configuration — set to 'full'
steps: Go to Slack, start a new thread mentioning the bot
Verify bot responds to all messages in the thread (not just mentions)
expected: With 'full' mode, bot responds to every message in a thread it's part of, not just direct mentions

name: Reply mode configuration — set to 'quiet'
steps: Go to Slack, in an active thread send a message WITHOUT mentioning the bot
expected: With 'quiet' mode, bot only responds to direct mentions in threads, stays silent on non-mention messages

name: Slack connection status indicator in dashboard
steps: Check for a connection status indicator
expected: Dashboard shows Slack connection status (connected/disconnected) clearly

name: Bot handles being removed from channel gracefully
steps: In Slack, remove the bot from the test channel
Try to send a message mentioning the bot
Re-add the bot to the channel
Send another message mentioning the bot
expected: Bot handles removal gracefully (no crash). After being re-added, bot resumes responding to messages

name: Dashboard shows Slack channel info after connection
steps: Check what information is displayed about the connected Slack workspace
expected: Dashboard shows relevant info: workspace name, bot name, connection status, possibly connected channels

name: Auth failure does not cause crash loop
steps: Connect Slack with a previously valid but now revoked/expired token
Or: connect, then revoke the bot token from api.slack.com
Check API logs for crash loop behavior
Check if the agent remains functional (dashboard still works, can chat)
expected: Agent does NOT enter an infinite restart/crash loop. Auth failure is handled gracefully. Agent remains functional for other tasks

name: Concurrent thread messages don't corrupt cache
steps: Open two browser tabs with different Slack users (or use API)
In the same thread, have both users send messages simultaneously
Wait for bot responses to both
Verify thread context is intact for subsequent messages
expected: Both messages handled without thread cache corruption. Bot can still follow thread context after concurrent messages

name: Bot responds to DM without channel membership
steps: Search for the bot by name
expected: Bot responds to DMs regardless of which channels it's added to

name: Verify analytics event fires on Slack connect
steps: After connecting Slack, check PostHog or API logs
expected: PostHog event 'agent_connected_to_channel' fires with correct properties including channel type 'slack'

name: Slack setup form on mobile viewport
steps: Verify the setup form is usable at mobile width
expected: Slack setup form is accessible and usable on mobile viewport — fields don't overflow, buttons are tappable

name: Delete Slack app and verify cleanup
steps: Find the test app created in SLACK-003
Verify it no longer appears in the app list
expected: Slack app deleted cleanly from api.slack.com. Note: the dashboard connection may still show as 'connected' until next auth attempt — verify this behavior

name: Existing Slack app — use pre-existing tokens
preconditions: An existing Slack app already created for this project
steps: Navigate to api.slack.com/apps and open the existing app
Get the App Token from Basic Information → App-Level Tokens
Get the Bot Token from OAuth & Permissions
Use these in the dashboard to connect
expected: Can connect using pre-existing app tokens without creating a new app. Useful for quick reconnection testing

name: Bot handles file/image shared in channel
steps: In the test channel, upload a small image or file
Mention the bot: '@BotName what is this file?'
expected: Bot either processes the file (if file handling is supported) or responds gracefully indicating it received a file. No crash or error

name: Bot handles edited messages
steps: In DM with bot, send a message: 'What is 2+2?'
Edit the original message to: 'What is 3+3?'
Check if bot responds to the edit or ignores it
expected: Bot either responds to the edit or ignores it gracefully. No crash or duplicate response

name: Bot handles deleted messages
steps: In DM with bot, send a message
Quickly delete the message before bot responds (or after)
Verify bot doesn't crash or enter error state
expected: Bot handles message deletion event gracefully. No crash, no error in logs

name: Slack replyToMode defaults to 'all'
expected: replyToMode defaults to 'all' for new Slack connections

name: Multiple agents sharing same Slack workspace
steps: Create a second agent in dashboard
Connect second agent to Slack with different app/bot tokens
Send messages to each bot in Slack
expected: Both agents function independently on the same Slack workspace without interference

name: Websocket reconnection after network interruption
steps: Verify bot is connected and responding in Slack
SSH to API server and restart the container
Send a message to the bot in Slack
expected: Bot reconnects to Slack after API restart and resumes handling messages. May take up to 30s
